title: No widget, no can do
body: I so wish this app had a widget option. If you are making an app for people with ADHD, a widget is not a "nice to have"—it is a life support system for many of us. “Out of sight, out of mind” is not just a saying for us; it is a neurological reality (it’s an object permanence thing). Unless my to-do list is in a widget on my Home Screen, it simply ceases to exist. As will your app. I will forget I downloaded it. I will forget I paid for it. I will forget I even have a phone. Please, give us widgets. Save us from ourselves.

author: IrishAce PDX

title: It’s nice to feel seen - or it would have been
body: A lot of people with chronic pain or autoimmune disorders have cognitive impairments related to their diagnosis. Come to think of it, I’ve heard the same about cancer survivors for years (or forever) after chemotherapy. I’m seeking help with a form of that known as “fibro fog”. I just set up my first task, cleaning the living room - that’s the project that has been top of my list for the last three months. I told the AI to double the time estimates and it did - that’s great! …But I’m still a long ways away from having a list that looks realistic or doable. If that sounds like an impossible situation, well, it is, but I think that it’s within reach for the intake questionnaire to accommodate people in my situation. Ask some version of “preferred Pomodoro intervals” (for me, that’s 45 minutes of rest for every 15 minutes of work) and “number of Pomodoros per day” (for me, 2). That means that, for me, cleaning the living room is actually four tasks spread out over two days - tidy, dust (dry), clean (wet), and vacuum/sweep. If I could do that much, I’d still be in an impossible situation, but I would also be way better off than I am right now.

Overall, it has potential but it just needs to work out the kinks before it can be a good app. I would consider maybe looking at other popular productivity apps (e.g. Structured) and seeing what they do.

title: Great app 10/10. Needs sharing across devices.
body: This app is very helpful with those with ADHD or those struggling with executive functioning. The AI tool that helps chunk and break down the main task is very helpful and accurate. The breakdown or how chunked the subtask are is based on the difficulty of the task you input. The easier or harder the task will correlate.This is  good for those with ADHD as it breaks it into smaller written task preventing overwhelm by one daunting task.  Only issue is hopefully in a future update there is cross saving and synchronization across devices. I haven’t fully explored but using the free version hasn’t interfered with using the app. If you have ADHD or struggle with procrastination or feeling overwhelmed please try this app.
author: Loha_Logan

title: Has potential
body: I'll start with the positive.  It's a good idea.  The AI creates subtasks so I don't have to, which can make things easier on my already overtaxed brain.  It is helpful to see how much extra time it's taken me to compete a certain step.  I'll admit though.  I bought this app, but don't use it. My number one complaint is that when the time is up for certain step of a task it sends a notification to my phone.  That's it.  I have an iPhone so all I get is a little ding.  I don't hear it or notice it, because I'm involved in an activity. I have ADHD, I forget the app is even running.  I need an alarm to go off, preferably one I can set to go off multiple times until I finish the step.  Another feature I'd like is the ability to have multiple tasks going at once.  I can only have one going at a time.  This is not ideal.  I gave it three stars because I hope it gets better.  Just a few small improvements would truly make this great.

author: Disappointed Sad———

title: My mental wheelchair
body:
this app is so helpful to me.  I had TBI and permanent brain damage in frontal lobe making my executive function and ADHD unmanageable.

Before my injury I was a “DataSmith” but after lost all hope, interest, motivation to claw my back.
Neurolist is my mental “wheelchair “ and given me hope.

Thank you for making my life more manageable.  The folks around me thank you too because it’s usefulness has alleviated other collateral damage from my accident, especially depression.

God bless, keep it up!

Rocket Queen 
A Neurolist ambassador
author: Rocket.Queen.19

title: Intelligent AI tool
body: I have ADHD and I downloaded this months ago as it seemed like a good tool to use to manage myself. I of course didn’t use it at first because of course (ADHD). But I asked for constant reminders to use it and have always gotten them. I finally put my foot down to clean my room and created a task for it and it created subtasks to make things easier. You can change the length of them, the difficulty of the task itself, and set a reminder. The AI subtask creator can do a multitude of tasks as well like a PC Build, Feeding your Animal, and more. Any task you create it will generate subtasks for it. Thank you for constantly reminding me to use it, and I finally have.

title: Seems good-needs a prioritization feature

The app needs a  way for us to color-code/sort tasks by high priority, medium priority, low priority so everything isn’t lumped together in the same way. otherwise i find it be confusing/overwhelming and can’t figure out where to start. The AI could also “suggest” prioritizing if we’re unsure, maybe putting work tasks or chores like grocery and cleaning first.
